relevance_note: Case report of a single boy with A20 haploinsufficiency caused by a novel de novo TNFAIP3 nonsense variant, described as 'the heterozygous substitution NM_006290.3:c.1084C > T was found', with individual-level clinical detail.
method_note: Read the paper, schema and rules directly; no script transcribed anything, so every span was checked character-for-character against the Markdown with searches (the file contains thin spaces U+2009 and four-per-em spaces U+2005 inside strings such as 'c.1084C > T', '113 mg/L' and '0.5 mg once per day'; those are reproduced exactly). Scope: the single patient of the case report plus the two parents, who are relatives described in relation to him and were tested for the variant (family segregation analysis, both negative), plus the two children of the earlier case report cited as (8), for whom the paper gives individual-level facts (ages 3 years and 6 months and a feature). The group-level summaries of earlier work (first cohort of 16 patients, ref 4; 61 patients of Yu et al., ref 6) give no individual-level data and got no rows. Labels: the paper gives the patient no label (only role words such as 'our patient' and 'the child'), so the rule-5 label 'patient' was used; the parents are named as 'mother' and 'father' separately in the text, so 'mother of patient' and 'father of patient' were used rather than 'parent of patient'. Tables 1 and 2 (flow cytometry, T cell differentiation) are laboratory tables for this one patient, not per-patient tables; their converted cells contain stacked values (e.g. 'C / %') and were not read positionally, so no value was taken from them - the narrative statements were used instead. Contradictions/tensions found: (a) the Discussion says 'He was having abdominal pains, recurrent diarrhea, and fever attacks since early infancy, from the age of 2 years old', whereas the case presentation says 'Fevers started at 7 weeks of age' and abdominal attacks started 'From the age of 2.5 years' - the earlier onset was recorded; (b) growth: 'Due to intrauterine growth retardation' vs 'His growth and weight were normal although on the lower percentiles' and 'Growth and development are so far normal' - both phenotypic rows were emitted and the checklist item 'growth failure' was set to not reported; (c) 'Abdominal ultrasound and magnetic resonance enterography did not show any signs of inflammation' was recorded as an excluded feature while 'Histology revealed non-specific mild inflammatory changes' and the elevated CRP were recorded as observed (different modalities, no direct contradiction). Normal/negative findings were recorded as excluded rows for the abnormality they rule out (e.g. ANA negative -> 'positive ANA'); these are largely differential diagnoses (cystic fibrosis, chronic granulomatous disease, celiac disease) or tests, not HA20 features, and a normal finding as a whole (imaging) was kept in the paper's own words. Per the composite-item rule, 'no arthritis', 'no rash' and negative ANA were not used to mark the checklist items 'arthritis or arthralgia', 'skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)' or 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)'. In silico predictions (CADD, MutationTaster, absent from dbSNP/gnomAD) were not treated as functional evidence, so functional_evidence_statement is not reported. The protein reference NP_006281.1 has no field in the schema and is not recorded. Age at diagnosis is not stated; vital status is not explicitly stated and was left not reported. Variant type 'nonsense' follows the authors' own description of a stop/termination codon and 'truncating mutation'.

span: After the result of genetic testing, in November 2018, the child started colchicine therapy at a dose of 0.5 mg once per day.
In January 2019, the dose was increased to 0.5 mg twice per day.
Our patient responded well to colchicine and so far did not need additional treatment.
